one_line_contribution: The claim that where a distilled agent-memory item should live (merged into the always-on instruction vs left in a retrieval-gated bank) is decided by a label-free coverage statistic — the fraction of unlabeled deployment queries for which the item enters top-k — and that the payoff of promotion is the top-k slot it vacates for narrow items, not the promoted text itself.
closest_prior_work: Two bodies the proposal never names. (1) Hubness in high-dimensional nearest-neighbour retrieval: b(m) is exactly the k-occurrence statistic N_k(m) of Radovanovic et al. (JMLR 2010), and the known pathology is that a few hub vectors enter the top-k of almost every query and crowd out relevant neighbours. The established remedies — hub demotion, local/global score centering, mutual-proximity, CSLS — remove the crowding without any instruction tier, so the proposal's central mechanism has a documented cause and a documented cheaper fix. Adjacent to it, Maximal Marginal Relevance (Carbonell & Goldstein 1998) and result diversification already solve 'a fixed-size result set is wasted on redundant, always-ranked items.' (2) ACE-style agentic context engineering and Mem0-style consolidation already perform grow-and-refine with semantic de-duplication of a growing always-on block, which is operationally 'consolidate the broad, keep the narrow retrievable' without the theory. MemGPT and working-set estimation are correctly conceded. Note also that the Related Work's load-bearing novelty argument — 'fast-tier residency does not free slow-tier capacity' — is false for exclusive cache hierarchies (Wong & Wilkes, DEMOTE, USENIX 2002), where promotion is precisely eviction from the lower tier; the 'inverted optimal move' is therefore a weaker discriminator against caching theory than the proposal claims.
strongest_objection: The matched-token protocol is arithmetically incompatible with the mechanism the paper wants to demonstrate, and the incompatibility loads the headline test. Arm E2 (vi) is base prompt + consolidated block C + k retrieved items with freed slots refilled; arm E2 (ii) is base prompt + k retrieved items. The hybrid is strictly longer by |C|, so 'mean realized prompt tokens within 5%' can only be achieved by inflating pure top-k — either raising its k, or appending the neutral filler of ablation (e). Both inflations are already known from this track's own pilot to be harmful: cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank, i.e. injection volume is the established causal lever. So a >=3 EM win for the hybrid over pure top-k (P2) is predicted by the volume effect alone, with zero placement content, and the paper would be re-deriving its own starting position under a new name. E3's padding control does not rescue this, because it pads the hybrid's freed slots rather than testing a token-matched no-consolidation arm. Compounding this, P2 anchors the hybrid only against pure top-k and pure playbook: given a pilot in which the full bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven, the hybrid can satisfy every one of P2, P3, P4 and P5 while still losing to the no-memory arm that E2 (i) runs but no prediction references — a placement law that is beaten by having no memory at all is vacuous, and nothing in the pre-registration forecloses that outcome.
what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes. (1) State the token-matching operator explicitly and pre-register it: match by holding the retrieval slot count k identical across arms and equalizing tokens with a token-matched drop-only-plus-filler arm, and report the accuracy-versus-tokens curve as primary rather than any single matched point; if matching is done by raising k for the baseline, the contrast must be pre-declared as confounded with volume. (2) Add a pre-registered superiority test of the breadth hybrid against the no-memory arm at matched tokens, and state up front that failure to clear no-memory voids P2-P5 regardless of their internal outcomes. (3) Run E1 condition (c), item absent entirely, on all 14 items rather than 4, and regress the contrast acc(instr) - acc(absent) on b(m) alongside acc(instr) - acc(bank); as designed, the breadth coefficient in P1 is close to a tautology, since removing a broad item from the bank necessarily perturbs top-k on nearly every query while removing a narrow one perturbs almost none, so the current slope measures slot-vacating and cannot separate consolidation from deletion. (4) Fund the utility estimator to a precision at which it could win: 6 paired probes per item on 60 of 300 items leaves u(m) with a standard error on the order of the effects being routed on, and leaves 240 items with no utility value at all, so 'coverage beats utility' and 'utility is not a significant predictor after conditioning on breadth' are both largely guaranteed by estimator noise. Pre-register the diagnostic that if utility routing lands within noise of the random-routing arm in E4, the utility comparison is declared uninformative rather than won.
missing_baseline: Breadth-penalized (hub-demoted / MMR-diversified) fixed-k retrieval: leave every item in the bank and subtract a calibrated function of b(m) from the retrieval score, or apply standard hubness correction / MMR diversification, so narrow items surface into top-k without any instruction tier, any consolidation LLM call, or any extra tokens. This is the arm a retrieval-literate reviewer will demand, because it delivers the paper's own claimed mechanism — vacate the slot the broad item was occupying — at strictly lower token cost, and if it matches the hybrid the entire instruction-vs-bank placement framing collapses into a re-ranking heuristic. Drop-only (E3 c) is not a substitute: it deletes the item from the system entirely rather than demoting it, and it is not token-matched to the hybrid. Secondarily missing: a token-matched drop-only arm (broad items removed, no consolidated block, tokens padded to the hybrid's budget), which is the only clean isolation of what the consolidated text contributes.
preprint_collision: The check is not thin — it is empty, and the proposal says so: the web search tool failed on every invocation, zero titles or dates were retrieved, and the closest-work list is explicitly recollection. By the standard that an unsearched claim of novelty is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is the single largest deduction, and it is aggravated by the proposal's own note that two prior review rounds flagged it and it remains unfixed; the commitment to run a dated search log before submission is a promise, not evidence. The proposed query list is also blind in the direction where the real collision lives: it searches the agent-memory and context-engineering vocabulary but never the retrieval vocabulary (hubness, k-occurrence, hub reduction, result diversification, MMR, redundancy-aware re-ranking), which is where the coverage statistic and its standard remedy already exist. I cannot name a specific mid-2025-to-present preprint that runs the refill/no-refill/padding controls, so the mechanism controls plausibly remain unclaimed; but the decision problem is MemGPT's, the statistic is working-set estimation applied to a hubness quantity, and dedup-under-capacity of an always-on playbook is already implemented in ACE-lineage and Mem0-style consolidation systems, so the residual novelty surface is much narrower than the proposal asserts and remains unverified.
